plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs light up the cold winter landscape with rose-like blooms. Each flower has layers of satiny petals around a golden boss of stamens. They stand out against dark, leathery leaves, often while frost still dusts the garden.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter to early spring (roughly January to March)
plants.location: Coastal woodlands and gardens of Japan, including Honshu and Kyushu
plants.funFact: In Japan, camellias are traditionally pollinated by birds such as the Japanese white-eye, which sip nectar while most insects are dormant.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, bare stems rise from clumps of strappy leaves, each topped with a rounded burst of trumpet-shaped flowers. In midsummer gardens the blue globes sway above the foliage and draw bees all day long.
plants.location: Gardens and roadsides across southern Australia, and native to South Africa's southern and eastern coasts
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily. Its name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower'.

plants.name: Prunus campanulata
plants.description: Long before the famous spring cherry blossoms, this tree covers itself in nodding, bell-shaped flowers of deep magenta-pink. People gather under it for winter flower-viewing picnics, enjoying early blossoms in mild island air.
plants.location: Okinawa and the Ryukyu Islands of Japan, and Taiwan
plants.funFact: Its blooming begins in the south and moves north. Okinawa's cherry blossom front is the earliest in Japan, and it runs opposite to the usual north-to-south timing of cherry blossoms.
